# Graph DSL: common grammar

Graph DSL is an S-expression language for reading and editing graph assets. The syntax
below is shared by every domain; each domain adds its own forms and node types.
`Docs` returns this common grammar together with your toolset's own dialect reference
in one call. Read it before authoring. `Schema` returns one node type's pins, properties,
and accepted value types as a `(node ...)` form. It accepts either the plain type name or
a backtick-delimited call head copied from DSL. Query unfamiliar node types instead of
guessing their shape.

## Forms

A form is an atom, an array `[values...]`, or a parenthesized list. Most lists begin with
a symbol head followed by positional arguments and `:key value` pairs. Forms can nest.
In syntax summaries, `...` means repetition and angle-bracketed words are placeholders.
Square brackets are literal when they show an array or comment color tag; surrounding
prose explicitly identifies optional syntax.

## Literals

- Symbols: bare words and keywords (`Add`, `:Alpha`).
- Strings: double-quoted, with `\"` and `\\` escapes (`"hello"`).
- Integers: `42`, `-7`. Floats: `3.14`, `1.0`, `.5`, `1e5`.
- Booleans: `true`, `false`.
- Arrays: `[a b c]`: an ordered list of values (used for positions, vectors, lists).

## Names

A name owned by the graph rather than by the DSL is written inside backticks.
Node types, pin and property labels, and the names of events, parameters, and variables
are all such names. Reads emit them delimited and writes must supply them the same way,
even when the name is one plain word: the delimiters are what say "this is a name,
resolve it" instead of "this is a literal value". A delimited name may contain spaces
and punctuation. Inside the delimiters, write a backtick as \` and a backslash as \\;
nothing else needs escaping. A leading ':' still gives the form keyword semantics, so it
cannot begin an ordinary graph-owned name.

    (bind Sample (`Get Actor Location` :`Target` `Spawner`))

So three kinds of word are spelled three ways:
- Grammar words and fixed dialect keywords stay bare: `bind`, `wire`, `if`, and `:!pos`.
- Graph-owned names are delimited, as above.
- Names the document introduces normally stay bare: a `bind` target and every later
  reference to it. `(bind Sample ...)` is consumed as ``:`Pin` Sample``. A dialect may
  delimit a local name that cannot be written as one safe bare atom.

The separate `Scope` argument uses the same backtick escapes when a segment needs quoting.

When a domain derives a node type from editor text, it uses the language-independent source
spelling rather than localized display text. Changing the editor language does not change
the DSL identifier.

## bind

``(bind Name (`NodeType` ...))`` creates a local name for a node's output. Other forms use
`Name`, bare, where they consume that output. Dialect references explain how to select a
particular output when a node has more than one.

## Node calls

A typical node call is ``(`NodeType` positional-args... :`Pin` value :`Property` value ...)``.
The dialect determines which positional arguments, pins, and properties a node accepts.
These keyword names belong to the node, not to Graph DSL grammar, so they are delimited.
In data-flow dialects, `(wire Ref...)` in a keyword's value slot is an explicit ordered
edge list: several sources into one pin, or an edge that a bare value could not mean.

## Metadata keywords (`:!`)

`:!`-prefixed keywords are shared metadata, never pins or properties:
- `:!pos [x y]`: node position. Reads omit it unless positions are requested; when absent,
  domains that use positions lay out nodes automatically on write.
Use only metadata documented here or by the dialect. Unknown or unsupported metadata is
ignored with a warning; a recognized keyword with an invalid value may fail the operation.
`:!delete` is valid only on a top-level entry tombstone, described below.

## Comments

- An own-line `; text` starts a persistent comment-box run. Each dialect defines which
  following forms belong to that run. Consecutive headers at the same semicolon depth form
  one multi-line label; changing depth starts a separate nested header. An optional leading
  `[r g b]`, `[r g b a]`, or `[r g b a size]` tag sets the box color and, with the fifth
  slot, its title font size. Color components are numeric and normally use the 0-1 range.
- The leading semicolon count is the nesting depth: a `;;` header opens a box inside
  the current `;` box; its run ends at the next header of the same or shallower depth.
- Comment boxes are represented by these text runs; box identity is not preserved.
- `; text` trailing a node-producing form on the same line is that node's note (the comment
  bubble). In note text, `\n` encodes a newline and `\\` a literal backslash, so a
  multi-line note stays on one line.

## References

Reference spelling depends on the dialect and destination type. The case-sensitive
prefixes `obj:`, `class:`, and `soft:` may identify a reference kind. Consult the dialect
reference for when a path must be a string literal or carry a prefix.

## Containers and entries

Each domain declares the top-level list heads it accepts. The `Scope` argument to `Read`,
`Write`, and `Edit` selects a dialect-specific subdocument.

Top-level entry writes use upsert semantics: entries present in the document are applied,
while omitted entries are kept and listed in a warning. A partial document can therefore
edit one entry without carrying the rest. Deletion is always explicit: write a tombstone
with the entry's own head, ``(head `Name` :!delete)``. For example,
``(event `Foo` :!delete)`` or ``(subgraph `Bar` :!delete)``. A
tombstone takes no body; deleting a missing entry warns and changes nothing; a
document may not both define and delete the same entry. Deletion and the remaining write
share one transaction; any resulting error rolls back the entire operation.

## Scope

A scope is a `/`-separated chain of non-empty segment names; the empty scope is the
whole asset. A segment whose text holds a space, syntax character, or a literal `/`
is backtick-quoted as one atom, the same convention a DSL body uses for a graph-owned
name: a graph named `A/B` is addressed as `` `A/B` ``, and one named `My Graph` as
`` `My Graph` ``. Plain names need no quoting. Each dialect defines what a
segment names (a graph, an entry, or a subgraph) and how deep a chain may go.

## Read / edit / write workflow

1. `Read` returns canonical DSL and a revision for one asset and scope.
2. `Edit` applies exact replacements to the last result for that same asset and scope. Each
   old string must be non-empty and unique unless `bReplaceAll` is true. Pass the revision
   from the latest `Read`, `Write`, or `Edit`. If the asset changed, call `Read` again.
3. `Write` applies the supplied document using the upsert rules above.
Errors report one item per problem; each item line begins with a stable bracketed
code such as `[unknown-pin]` identifying the failure kind, followed by the detail.
Graph mutation is transactional: any error leaves the graph unchanged. A successful
mutation returns a fresh revision and canonical DSL unless `bDslOmitted` is true, which
means the text you already hold matches the canonical result byte-for-byte. Use that text
and the returned revision as the baseline for the next `Edit`.

# Dialect: blueprint

BLUEPRINT DIALECT

Blueprint graphs combine statement exec flow with data expressions. Preserve graph-owned names
exactly as Read returns them.

NODE NAMES

Function and variable call heads are references (`Owner.Member`, or `self.Member` for this
Blueprint's class chain). A few built-in forms use `|` (`|MakeArray`, `Timeline|Name`,
`AddComponent|Name`, and entry families such as `Key|F5`). BlueprintToolset's palette type ids
(`Category|Name`, for example `Development|PrintString`) are not DSL call heads. Use
FindNodeReferences to look a reference up, and Schema to see its pins.

ENTRIES

    (event `EventName` [(params ...)] stmt ...)
    (fn `FunctionName` [(params ...)] stmt ...)

An engine or interface override uses the implemented member reference:

    (event `self.ReceiveBeginPlay` ...)
    (event `SomeInterface.OnThing` ...)

A component-bound event uses `self.Component.Dispatcher`:

    (event `self.MeshComp.OnComponentHit` ...)

Custom events use a bare graph-owned name. Preserve an emitted `Custom|` prefix.

A handler whose own name differs from the function or event dispatcher supplying its parameters
uses `:!signature`:

    (event `HandleDied`
      :!signature `self.OnDied`
      (params (Damage))
      stmt ...)

    (event `GameplayCue.Bumper.Knock`
      :!signature `GameplayCueInterface.BlueprintCustomHandler`
      (params (EventType) (Parameters))
      stmt ...)

SIGNATURES

    (fn `Score`
      (params (Name :type TypeId :default Value) ...)
      (returns (Name :type TypeId) ...)
      (locals (Name :type TypeId :default Value) ...)
      stmt ...)

The sections follow the entry name and configuration keywords, each at most once and in this order.
`(returns ...)` declares a function's outputs and `(locals ...)` its local variables; neither fits
an `(event ...)`. A section that is present is the exact set: listed items are added or updated,
and unlisted ones are removed, so `(params)` removes every parameter. A section that is absent leaves
that part alone. A new item needs `:type`; a listed one is retyped when its `:type` names another
type, and its `:default` is set when it differs. The order of the section is the order of the
pins. Items match by name, so a renamed item is a removal plus an addition. A function's first
output adds its result node. `(fn ...)` still needs an existing function graph.

A signature the entry inherits stays read-only: an override, an interface function, a handler
with `:!signature`, or an event bound to a dispatcher. Its sections describe the live pins, a name
the entry lacks fails, and a mismatched `:type` or `:default` warns while the graph wins. Locals
are always the function's own.

A pin type is spelled as the editor words it, except that a class, struct, or enum is named the way
type references name it, followed by its kind: `Integer`, `Pawn Object Reference`,
`Vector Structure`, `/Game/Modes/E_Mode Enum`, `Array of Actor Object Reference`.

INPUT EVENTS

Input event names encode their family and identity:

    `Key|F5`
    `Key|Ctrl+Shift+F5`                   modifiers are part of the key's identity
    `InputAction|Fire`
    `InputAxis|MoveForward`
    `InputAxisKey|Gamepad_LeftX`
    `InputVectorAxis|Mouse2D`
    `InputTouch`
    `EnhancedInput|/Game/Input/IA_Move`   enhanced input action path

Each family names only what the editor's palette offers: `Key|` takes digital keys,
`InputAxisKey|` 1D axes, and `InputVectorAxis|` 2D and 3D axes, all bindable in Blueprints.
`InputAction|` and `InputAxis|` take mapping names from Project Settings > Input, and
`EnhancedInput|` an action asset in a mounted content folder. Two events of one key that differ in
modifiers are two events.

Events with several exec outputs use named sections before any trailing statements; trailing
statements join the sections' dangling ends:

    (event `Key|F5` :consume false
      (params (Key))
      (:`Pressed` (`KismetSystemLibrary.PrintString` "down"))
      (:`Released` (`KismetSystemLibrary.PrintString` "up")))

Configuration keywords are emitted only when non-default: `:consume`, `:paused`, and
`:overrideparent`. Omitted keys reset to defaults.

STATEMENTS

    (set `self.Member` value)
    (set `Owner.Member` target value)
    (add `self.Dispatcher` handler)
    (remove `self.Dispatcher` handler)
    (clear `self.Dispatcher`)
    (message `Interface.Function` target args...)
    (cast `Class` object (:`then` ...) (:`CastFailed` ...))
    (castclass `Class` class-value (:`then` ...) (:`CastFailed` ...))
    (setmembers `Struct` :`StructRef` target :`Member` value ...)
    (return [value ...])
    (if condition stmt ... [(elif condition stmt ...) | (else stmt ...)])
    (for item (range stop) stmt ...)
    (for item (range start stop) stmt ...)
    (for item array stmt ...)
    (for (item index) array stmt ...)
    (while condition stmt ...)
    (switch `Type` value (:`Case` stmt ...) ...)
    (break)
    (goto label)

`setmembers` changes only named members. `message` is a runtime-checked interface call; a plain
member call is direct. `elif` or `else` must end its enclosing branch. `break` exits the innermost
breakable loop. Range stops are exclusive.

`_` is a no-op statement. As an argument it leaves that pin unchanged, including an unspellable
struct default or by-reference parameter.

MULTI-EXEC CALLS

    (`NodeType` args...
      (:`ExecOut1` stmt ...)
      (:`ExecOut2` stmt ...))

Named exec sections follow data arguments. Trailing statements run after their continuations rejoin.
``(:`Pin`)`` leaves an output unwired; ``(:`Pin` _)`` connects it directly to the trailing statement.

Continuation bodies expose each data output as an implicit local: lowercase the pin name, replace
spaces with underscores, and prefix `_` (`Return Value` becomes `_return_value`). Bind the call to
use an output afterward. Bindings remain visible to later continuations and trailing statements.

MULTIPLE DATA OUTPUTS

An inline pure call selects its first data output. To select others, bind names to outputs in order:

    (bind (value found) (`BlueprintMapLibrary.Find` map key))

Use throwaway names for preceding outputs.

ANCHORED NODES

Timelines and add-component calls address existing nodes; a missing match is an error and omission
does not delete one. An anchored call owns the node's wiring; omitted keywords preserve live pin
values.

A timeline is one ``(`Timeline|Name` ...)`` statement with input keywords, output binds, and
continuations. It enters `Play` unless ``:!via `Pin` `` names another exec input. Other arrivals use
a goto to its label with the same `:!via`. Query Schema for available pins.

    (bind (_direction _fader) (`Timeline|FadeTimeline` :!via `PlayFromStart` :!label _fade)
      (:`Update` (`KismetMaterialLibrary.SetScalarParameterValue`
        :`ParameterName` "Fade" :`ParameterValue` _fader)))
    ...
    (goto _fade :!via `Reverse`)

``(`AddComponent|TemplateName` ...)`` addresses an existing add-component node. Each occurrence
claims one matching node.

EXPRESSIONS

    variable      Name
    arithmetic    (+ a b ...) (- a b ...) (* a b ...) (/ a b ...) (mod a b) (- value)
    comparison    (== a b) (!= a b) (< a b) (<= a b) (> a b) (>= a b)
                  (== a b :`ErrorTolerance` 0.01) names an input past the operands
    boolean       (and a b ...) (or a b ...) (xor a b) (not value)
    conditional   (select `Type` value :`Case` result ...)
Numeric literals preserve pin type: a real pin reads `0.0`, while an integer pin reads `0`. An
operator resolves from wired operands first, then Float or Bool literals. An Int literal uses the
width selected by other operands, or `int` when none selects one. `==` and `!=` on strings and text
ignore case; a string literal makes a string comparison when no other operand has a type. An exact
comparison calls `KismetStringLibrary.EqualEqual_StrStr` or `KismetTextLibrary.EqualEqual_TextText`.

Every bare non-literal atom is a local reference. Quote identifier-like values such as class paths,
enum values, and asset paths:

    "/Script/Engine.StaticMeshActor"
    "AlwaysSpawn"
    "/Game/Meshes/SM_Cube.SM_Cube"

Use `null` to clear an object, class, soft, or interface reference. The bare local `self` is the
owning Blueprint object; a parameter named `self` shadows it.

A plain string on a text pin writes new localizable text. ``(loctable "TableId" "Key")`` names a
string table entry instead, and a pin holding one reads back that way. It is valid only on a text pin
passed by value, and it spells Text where literals type a Select or Make container.

COMPONENT AND OUTPUT ACCESS

These fixed attributes lower to Break nodes:

    .x .y .z                    vector
    .pitch .yaw .roll           rotator
    .location .rotation .scale  transform

Any other `.Name` selects that output pin without creating a node. Reads use it for statement
outputs and visible optional members; pure calls use a multi-output bind instead.

STRUCT VALUES

Vector-family defaults use positional tuples; other structs use ``(struct :`Field` value ...)`` with
default-valued fields omitted:

    (1 2 3)
    (struct :`Yaw` 90)
    (struct :`Min` (1 2 3))

A Rotator uses `Pitch`, `Yaw`, and `Roll`; colors use their named channels. A struct value on a
by-reference pin splits and fills that pin. An incompatible struct form fails the write.

MEMBERS AND NODE TYPES

Members use `Owner.Member`. `self` means this Blueprint's class chain; another owner is a native
class name or Blueprint class path. Every member is spelled by its authored name, as Read returns it:
`K2_SetActorLocation`, not `SetActorLocation`. A variable of this Blueprint's own class chain that a
node reaches through a target pin is spelled with its class instead of `self`.

    (`self.UpdateScore` 5)
    (set `self.Health` 100)
    (`Actor.SetActorHiddenInGame` target true)
    (`/Game/Doors/BP_Door.Open` door)

Member references resolve on the named class, not through the palette. Function-local variables and
parameters use `local.Name` inside their function; only variables are writable. A function declares
its local variables in its `(locals (Name :type TypeId :default Value) ...)` section.

`parent.Function` calls the nearest parent class's implementation, as Super::Function does in C++:

    (`parent.ReceiveBeginPlay`)

Macros use their library asset or `self` as owner:

    (`/Engine/EditorBlueprintResources/StandardMacros.Gate`)
    (`self.MyMacro`)

Struct operations use a native struct name or struct asset path:

    (make `Margin` 1.0 2.0)
    (bind (_min _max) (break `Box` box))
    (setmembers `Margin` :`StructRef` target :`Top` 2.0)

A user-defined struct's members are named as the struct's editor shows them.

Class casts use the target class. Without `:!pure`, a cast is the exec cast: a bind takes the typed
value, statements after it run only on success, and a failed cast ends the flow unless a
``(:`CastFailed` ...)`` continuation handles it. `:!pure true` selects the pure cast, which has no
exec pins: a two-name bind takes value and success, and `bSuccess` may be selected. Casting an enum
reference is the byte-to-enum cast, which is always pure.

    (bind _pawn (cast `Pawn` object))
    (cast `Pawn` object (:`CastFailed` ...))
    (bind (_pawn _ok) (cast `Pawn` object :!pure true))
    (bind _reason (cast `EEndPlayReason` byte))

Enum operations are ``(enumliteral `Enum` "Entry")``, ``(enumcount `Enum`)``, and
``(foreach `Enum` (:`LoopBody` ...))``. Class defaults use ``(defaults `Class` [class-value])``.
Subsystem getters use ``(subsystem `SubsystemClass`)``; local-player subsystems use
``(pcsubsystem `SubsystemClass` controller)``.

Non-member nodes use a `|` token such as `|MakeArray` or `|FormatText`. Query Schema before using an
unfamiliar type. Format Text arguments may be keywords named after the format's `{Name}`
placeholders, in any order; with a wired format, the keywords create the argument pins.

SWITCHES

`int`, `string`, and `name` alias `|SwitchInteger`, `|SwitchString`, and `|SwitchName`; other heads
use a type reference. Integer cases are consecutive from the lowest. String and name case keywords
create their pin names. Gameplay-tag cases must be registered. `Default` names the default arm.

``(select `Type` value :`Case` result ...)`` uses `bool`, `int`, `byte`, or an enum reference as its
index type. Cases are `true`/`false`, numbers, or enum entries. An `int` or `byte` select lists every
numbered option. Read adds `:!type` when replaying the options would infer a different type, as with
literal-only options or options narrower than the Select's type.

BLUEPRINT METADATA

In addition to common metadata, Blueprint supports:

    :!pinned true              keep a node's note bubble visible
    :!event `Entry`            select the entry wrapped by `|CreateDelegate`
    :!type "Pin Type"          element type for `|MakeArray`, `|MakeSet`, `|MakeMap`,
                              `select`, or a macro with wildcard pins
    :!valuetype "Pin Type"     value type for `|MakeMap`
    :!label name               mark a statement as a goto target
    :!via `Pin`                enter a statement through an exec input other than its first
    :!pure true                select the pure form of a cast: no exec pins, value plus success
    :!signature `Owner.Member` select the parameter source of an event entry

Preserve emitted container type metadata; values alone may not replay to the same type. Type
annotations use the pin-type spelling above. `:!signature` is valid only on an event entry head.

COMMENT ATTACHMENT

Comment-box headers cover the next contiguous statement run in the same entry or nested body. A
trailing note attaches to a statement node or a bind's created node; node-free binds and control
forms cannot carry notes.

COLLAPSED GRAPHS

If Read expands a collapsed graph, a write that changes its entry permanently replaces the
collapsed node with flat nodes.

GOTO AND LABELS

Every node has one statement. An exec wire into a node owned by another chain or entry becomes a
goto:

    (`KismetSystemLibrary.PrintString` "tick" :!label target)
    (if (`KismetMathLibrary.RandomBool`) (goto target))

Place `:!label name` on a call or bind, or after an `if`, `for`, `while`, or `switch` signature.
Labels are graph-unique. Statements enter the first exec input unless ``:!via `Pin` `` names another;
gotos use the same annotation:

    (`/Engine/EditorBlueprintResources/StandardMacros.Gate` :!via `Open` :!label _gate)
    (for (_actor _i) (`self.Candidates`) :!label _scan (if (== _actor (`self.Target`)) (break)))
    (goto _gate)
    (goto _scan :!via `Break`)

Goto, return, and break terminate their statement chain.

STALE REFERENCES

`(stale name)` reads a bound value from another exec scope in the current entry;
``(stale `Entry` Name)`` reads a parameter or binding from another entry. It changes no execution
order and cannot be rebound.

DELEGATES

`|CreateDelegate` wraps an event or function named by `:!event`:

    (event `HandleDestroyed` :!signature `self.OnDestroyed`
      (params (DestroyedActor :type "Actor Object Reference")))

    (event `self.ReceiveBeginPlay`
      (add `self.OnDestroyed` (`|CreateDelegate` :!event `HandleDestroyed`)))

``(delegate `EntryName`)`` references a same-graph custom event's own delegate output.

BLUEPRINT SCOPES

    empty                     every event and function graph
    GraphName                 one graph
    GraphName/EntryName       one event or function entry

Writes create missing custom events, but function bodies require existing function graphs. Deleting
a referenced entry fails.

EXAMPLE

    (event `self.ReceiveBeginPlay`
      (bind loc (`Actor.K2_GetActorLocation`))
      (if (> (.z loc) 0)
        (for _ (range 5)
          (`KismetSystemLibrary.PrintString` "tick"))))
